note: Set A captures substantially more of the page's engineering content correctly — C8X11.5, W10X15, HSS4X4X1/4, L4X4X5/16, L3X3X1/4, PL 4 1/2X4 1/2X1/2, CONT. BENT PLATE 7.5X3X1/4, 1/4" stiff plates, T.O. STEEL 11'-4", FIRST FLR 2'-4" and the (2) 3/4" bolts — while Set B omits most of these. However, A is noisier: it repeats several facts (bolts, W10X15, HSS, T.O. STEEL, the 1/4" dimension three times) and misreads the drawing scale as a spacing and a grid letter as a cutting plane. Set B is cleaner but loses key facts and also misbinds the scale as "reinforcement spacing" and the 11"X3/8" CONT. SUPPORT PLATES as "reinforcement," plus reads a weld symbol as a slope. On balance A's much better coverage of the actual member and connection data outweighs its extra noise.
remarks: Text layer is in scrambled reading order and does not include the weld symbols (e.g. the triangle after 1/4"), so weld-size claims can only be verified from the image. Both sets make the same class of error: treating the detail scale '1 1/2" = 1'-0"' as a physical dimension (A: component spacing; B: reinforcement spacing) — it is a drawing scale only. Both also miss the 5"X3/8" CONT. SUPPORT PLATES, the 2'-9 1/16" and 3'-0" dimensions in Detail C5, and the 1 1/2" dimension near the C1/C5 bolted angles. Set A's quote '1 1/2" = 1'-0" C5 SOUT' is truncated and does not match the text layer.
